rooms.name: The River Ivlis
rooms.desc: Fifty feet of fast, glass-clear winter-blue water, every stone on the bed showing ten feet down; two ribs of rock foam white under the bridge, and a long slow pool lies still above them.
rooms.dm: 50 ft wide, 5-10 ft deep, very cold. Swimming: DC 10 Athletics in the Mirror Pool; DC 15 in the narrows, the elbow and the north channel, and a failure sweeps the swimmer 20 ft downstream per round toward the bar. The south channel at the bar is a 2-3 ft wade (difficult terrain, no check). Heavy armour: disadvantage. Every 10 minutes in the water: DC 10 Con save or a level of exhaustion from the cold. Fog lies on the water at dawn and dusk (lightly obscured).

rooms.name: The Shingle Bar
rooms.desc: A crescent of bone-white shingle, 140 ft long, with a spine of bleached stones and three rounded boulders. Everything the river brings down from the falls fetches up on its head; a wrecked farm wain lies in the gravel at its tail.
rooms.dm: The deep north channel against the bluff is fast (DC 15); the south channel is a wade the wolves use as their ford, never the bridge. The strand line, the wain and the undercut opposite hold the hidden finds. 15+ on d20 for encounters here.

objects.label: The Narrows: upper sill
objects.desc: A rib of bedrock just under the surface, a standing wave and a strip of white foam below it: the loudest water on the river.

objects.label: The Strand Line
objects.desc: Splintered timbers, a wagon wheel, bleached bones, rags and a torn boot, combed into one heap by the current on the head of the bar.

objects.label: The Drowned Wain
objects.desc: A farm wain that went off the ford in a flood, half buried in gravel, one shaft pointing at the sky, a wheel still turning in the current.

objects.label: Fish weir
objects.desc: Driven stakes and wicker panels angled across the shallow channel, a basket trap at the point; a cord runs up to a bell on the bank. A villager checks it at dawn.

objects.label: The Washing Stones
objects.desc: Flat slabs at the waterline with hollows worn into them by generations of beaten laundry; a drying pole with a forgotten rag, a basket. Every word spoken on the bridge is heard here.

objects.label: The Hollow Willow
objects.desc: An ancient pollarded willow, roots in the river, trunk split and hollow, its crown a fist of thick stubs where ravens sit in all weathers and watch the bridge.

objects.label: The Undercut
objects.desc: Where the fast channel runs hard against the bluff the current has eaten a hollow under it, roots hanging into black water. A sweetish rot drifts out when the wind backs east.

objects.label: The Mirror Pool
objects.desc: Above the sills the river backs up into a slow, glass-clear reach holding the only blue in the valley; the pillar of Castle Ravenloft stands over the pines to the north-west and hangs upside down in the water.

objects.label: Blue cloth and silver clasp
objects.desc: A strip of scorched blue cloth snagged in the timbers, a tarnished silver clasp of fine make still on it.
objects.dm: The wizard who was thrown from Tser Falls (p.37): the Vistani found no body because the Ivlis carried him off, and he is alive: the Mad Mage of Mount Baratok (area M, p.39).

objects.label: Strongbox under the wain bed
objects.desc: A small iron-bound box wedged under the wain's bed, buried in gravel.
objects.dm: DC 13 Perception from the bar, 10 minutes of digging: a few coins and one roll on the Trinkets table (the "trinket" encounter, p.32).

container.contents: A handful of worn coins, 2d10 cp and 1d6 sp, and one small odd keepsake (roll a trinket).

objects.label: The missing villager
objects.playerLabel: A pale shape under the roots
objects.desc: A man's body wedged under the roots below the waterline, torn about the throat and belly.
objects.dm: The villager the scouts are searching for (the "corpse" encounter, p.30), killed by dire wolves. DC 12 Perception from the bar to see him as a pale shape under the roots. The scouts recognise him.

objects.label: Wereraven's bundle
objects.desc: A leather-wrapped roll of drab Barovian common clothes stuffed into the hollow of the crown, twelve feet up.
objects.dm: A wereraven's clothes (the raven in the tree; p.31-32). Finding it and leaving it alone earns the Keepers' goodwill; on a second meeting the wereraven invites the party to the Blue Water Inn.

objects.label: Child's doll
objects.desc: Wedged in the hollow of the lowest washing slab: a child's wooden doll, waterlogged, one eye a nail head.
objects.dm: Flavour. A villager in E will claim it if asked.

objects.label: Swarm of bats (under the arch)
objects.playerLabel: A flutter of wings under the arch
objects.dm: Swarms of bats (1d8), night: they attack without provocation when a light is carried under the bridge or along the north bank below the bluff. One swarm is the castle's spy and tries to leave with a report (p.32, spies sidebar).

objects.label: Raven in the willow (spy or wereraven)
objects.dm: Always present by day. 50%: an ordinary spy of the castle (flees when noticed, tries to snatch a small item). 50%: a wereraven in raven form who keeps its distance, flies off when stared at and comes back; its bundle is in the hollow of the crown. Ravens carry lost souls, the Vistani say; killing one is bad luck (p.28).

objects.label: Will-o'-wisp over the pool
objects.playerLabel: A lantern light on the far bank
objects.dm: Night: it looks like a lantern on the far bank and leads anyone who follows onto the slick sills or into the deep water at the elbow.

objects.playerLabel: A shambling shape in the water
objects.dm: Zombies (3d6), night wilderness encounter: they wade upstream in the south shallows from the east edge and climb out over the bar; the water hides their smell until they reach it.

rooms.name: River Ivlis: the south terrace
rooms.desc: A low grass terrace runs along the south side of a clear, cold river, pines closing in behind it. Ahead the road climbs a long ramp onto a single tall stone arch; the water hisses white over rock under the bridge.
rooms.dm: Check for a random encounter every 30 minutes: 18+ on d20 on the road and bridge, 15+ on the bar, bank path or in the water; skip it after two outdoor encounters in 12 hours. The village (E) is a mile north by the road; the crossroads (F) two miles south-west; the Tser Pool camp (G) two miles up the bank path. Vistani escorts take the path, not the bridge.

rooms.name: The north meadow
rooms.desc: North of the river the bank stands up as a grey rock lip over the water, and open meadow climbs away toward the village. A scored standing stone marks the bridgehead; a cluster of rounded boulders sits on a knoll above the bar.
rooms.dm: The north bluff is 7 ft of layered rock over the water. From the Sheep Rocks a watcher sees the whole road from edge to edge and the ford; anyone there is hidden from the bridge with cover. Scouts stage here.

objects.label: The Wolf Gibbet
objects.desc: A 14-ft pole with a crossbar at the foot of the ramp, hung with a dozen wolf skulls, dried pelts and rusted trap chains: the trappers' tally, knocking together in the wind.

objects.label: The Flood Stone
objects.desc: A man-high squared stone on the bluff lip, its river face scored with eight horizontal lines and old numerals, the top one above your head; the name IVLIS cut in worn capitals and a half-effaced device above.

objects.label: Flood Stone: each line is a past flood; the name is the old family of the castle crypts (Ivliskova, Ivliskovich, p.89-90).
The Sheep Rocks
objects.desc: Five rounded lichen-grey boulders, the largest eight feet high, on a knoll above the bluff: cover for anyone watching the road and the ford.

objects.label: Tracks in the mud
objects.desc: Hoof prints of draft horses pressed into the mud slope and, over them, the broad pads of very large wolves.

objects.label: The Drinking Slope: animals come down to drink here, 50 ft off the road. The hooves are the Vistani camp's draft horses (G); the pads over them are dire wolves.
The Trappers' Hide
objects.desc: A low blind of brush and wicker hurdles facing the ford, a floor of trodden pine needles, a cold fire ring, two crossbow bolts stuck in the sod.

objects.label: Weir bell
objects.desc: A small bronze bell on a stake; its cord runs down into the river to the fish weir. It creaks when the current pulls.

objects.label: Hunting trap (set)
objects.desc: A rusted steel-jaw trap set in the ford exit under a skin of pine needles.
objects.dm: Front rank DC 15 Survival to spot; otherwise one random character steps in it: 1d4 piercing and the leg is held (DC 13 Str to pull free, 1d4 more). The trappers set them to thin the wolves; the castle's wolves are too clever for them.

objects.label: South-west along the road: the gallows crossroads (F), 2 miles, 40 minutes. Tser Falls (H) 4 miles by road through F.
North along the road: the village of Barovia (E), 1 mile, about 20 minutes on foot.
The bank path runs north-west along the pool through the pines to the Tser Pool camp (G): 2 miles, 45-60 minutes of rough going.
Barovian scout (in the hide)
objects.dm: Barovian scouts (1d6): hunters and trappers searching for a missing villager; daytime road encounter, 18+ on d20. Passive Perception 16+ spots one figure. Once they see the party is no threat they lower their crossbows and ask for help. The man they want is in the Undercut.

objects.label: Skeletal rider on a skeletal warhorse
objects.dm: Night or day road encounter: comes down the north road out of the fog, crosses the bridge at a walk and rides on south-west toward the crossroads, holding up a rusted lantern that sheds no light. Ignores the party unless attacked (p.31). Skeleton statistics for the rider; warhorse skeleton for the mount.

objects.playerLabel: A Vistani by a small fire
objects.dm: Vistani bandits (1d4+1), daytime: laughter and pipe smoke reach the bridge first. They are picking over the strand line for valuables and offer themselves as guides for 100 gp (p.32).

objects.label: A small fire
objects.desc: A small fire of driftwood by the bank path, a clay pipe left on a stone beside it; the smoke drifts out over the pool.

rooms.name: The Village Bridge
rooms.desc: A single tall arch of grey stone carries the road sixteen feet over the narrows, its waist-high parapets furred with moss on every north face; a drain spout dribbles green below. From the deck you look straight up one reach of the river and straight down the other.
rooms.dm: Safe to cross and wide enough for a wagon. A fall from the deck is 16 ft into 10 ft of water: DC 12 Dex save to miss the sill, 1d6 bludgeoning on a failure, and the swimmer is in the narrows (DC 15). Anything said here is heard plainly at the washing stones below; Perception to hear anything else over the sills is at disadvantage within 60 ft. Looking up the pool (bearing 331) the castle stands over the right-hand pines and hangs upside down in the water; after dusk one window shows a light, in the water first.

objects.label: Tally marks
objects.desc: Low on the downstream parapet, where a child could reach: eleven short strokes and one word in Barovian.
objects.dm: The word is "hanged". Someone counted the eleven unmarked graves at the crossroads two miles back (F). Flavour.

objects.label: Sight line up the pool (bearing 331): the castle over the right-hand pines, 2.3 miles off and a thousand feet up, mirrored in the water.
